insights.summary: From the September 2026 AGM presentation: Q1 FY27 total income rose 49% to ₹178 Cr with a 40.8% EBITDA margin and PAT of ₹39 Cr, below the war-boosted Q4 but 10% above Q3 FY26. The fleet is still three 737 freighters (the third only joined in June), the two more promised by Q2 are described as 'planned', and the Boeing 777s are now presented as a 'future' long-haul strategy for a Japan/Korea-India-Africa corridor. A ₹200 Cr QIP in May took money raised since listing to ~₹479 Cr; cash was ₹153 Cr at June.

what_changed.text: Fourth and fifth 737s still 'planned' (promised before Q2)
Boeing 777s described as a future, 'proposed' aircraft
Corridor strategy: Japan/Korea/ASEAN to Africa via Chennai and Dubai

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: AFCOM's long-haul strategy is not aspirational geography, it is a distance the proposed aircraft type is built to fly.

red_flags.text: Fleet expansion behind the timeline given in June; no new dates in the AGM deck.
Much of the deck is industry statistics and an 'illustrative' route network rather than firm plans.
Q1 revenue fell 8% from Q4 as war charters faded.
Repeated equity raises (~₹479 Cr since 2024 listing).
